scope: KandyDrops security, rules, and role-boundary launch audit

launchCriticalFixes.summary: Protected the admin analytics redirect route with explicit admin auth.
Closed direct Firebase Storage client read/write access to drops/** and moved Drop asset upload through server-guarded admin/creator routes.

auditTable.currentGuard: Client AdminLayout requires Firebase user and userProfile.role === "admin" before rendering admin children.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only; non-admin authenticated users redirect to their preferred authenticated path; guests redirect home.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A non-admin may request the shell bundle, but protected data still comes from admin-guarded API and Firestore lanes.
auditTable.testRequired: Validator checks the admin layout role gate and redirect path.

auditTable.currentGuard: Every admin API route has auth: "admin" or verifyAdmin through guardApiRequest.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only; state-changing routes also require trusted origin.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A stolen user token without admin role cannot call admin APIs; cross-site POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE calls are rejected by trusted-origin checks.
auditTable.requiredFix: Fixed missing admin guard on /api/admin/analytics redirect route.
auditTable.testRequired: npm run check:security-role-boundaries and admin route tests.

auditTable.currentGuard: Explicit guardApiRequest auth: "admin" before redirecting to realtime or historical analytics lanes.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only for all admin analytics entrypoints.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Before this pass, a caller could hit the redirect shim without an explicit admin guard and rely on downstream routes for protection.
auditTable.requiredFix: Added guardApiRequest with auth: "admin" and route test coverage.

auditTable.currentGuard: Admin auth on all lanes; refresh POST requires trusted origin and preserves private no-store response behavior.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only; refresh is state-changing and must reject untrusted origin.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Normal users or guests attempting to read analytics/debug data receive auth failure; CSRF refresh attempts fail origin checks.
auditTable.requiredFix: None beyond the prior readiness trusted-origin fix.
auditTable.testRequired: admin analytics route tests and security role-boundary validator.

auditTable.currentGuard: Admin auth; debug write/preference/fix routes require trusted origin.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only, with technical diagnostics never public-readable.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A non-admin cannot read route names, parity details, diagnostics, or trigger assistant repair actions.
auditTable.testRequired: admin debug route tests and validator.

auditTable.currentGuard: Admin auth and trusted origin; uploads and deletes use Firebase Admin Storage under drops/.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Admin actor only for content library mutation.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Only admin can mint Drop asset URLs or delete Drop assets through server-side validation.
auditTable.requiredFix: Admin Drop asset uploads now use this route instead of direct client Storage writes.

auditTable.currentGuard: Direct client get/list/write are false; Drop assets are uploaded and served through server routes.
auditTable.expectedGuard: No direct client access because object paths do not encode entitlement.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Before this pass, any signed-in user who guessed a drops/** path could ask the client SDK for a download URL or write arbitrary Drop assets.
auditTable.requiredFix: Set drops/** get/write to false and added server upload routes for admin and creator Drop assets.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin user must have creator role and no dropSubmissionsRestricted flag; Firebase Admin Storage writes under drops/creator-submissions/{uid}.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Creator actor only for creator-submitted draft Drop assets.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Creator asset upload no longer depends on broad Storage write rules for all signed-in users.
auditTable.requiredFix: Added server-side creator Drop asset upload route.

auditTable.currentGuard: Admin client read only; direct client writes false; public Drop browsing goes through sanitized server read models.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Guests and users can see public-safe Drop data only through API/server surfaces, never raw Firestore docs.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A public user cannot query raw drop docs that may include content URLs or operational fields.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin caller must either own the creatorId or have dropId in unlockedContent; response is private no-store proxy stream.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Entitled user or creator owner only.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A user without unlock cannot stream protected content even if they know the drop id.
auditTable.requiredFix: Storage rules were hardened so this proxy is the only client path to Drop content.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin user; Firestore transaction reads server balance/source split and applies idempotent unlockedContent update.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Authenticated user only, server-authoritative balance, no client balance authority.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A repeated unlock returns existing entitlement without double charge; insufficient server balance blocks the unlock.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin user; create validates package price; capture validates PayPal completion, custom_id user/package binding, payment lock, and server ledger transaction.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Purchase completion must be server-confirmed and idempotent.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Client cannot self-credit Gum Drops or complete another user's PayPal order.

auditTable.currentGuard: Self or admin read; direct client writes false.
auditTable.expectedGuard: A user can read their own profile; admin can inspect users; all writes go through server routes.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A user cannot read another user's private profile or write wallet/role fields directly.

auditTable.currentGuard: Self or admin read; direct client writes false.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Transactions are server-written and visible only to owner/admin.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Users cannot fabricate wallet, purchase, or unlock ledger rows.

auditTable.currentGuard: Recipient read only by resource.data.userId; direct client writes false.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Notification records are visible only to intended recipient through rules and API filters.
auditTable.exploitScenario: One user cannot directly read another user's notification document.

auditTable.currentGuard: GET/PUT use authenticated trusted-origin user and visibility checks; POST uses admin auth and trusted origin.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Recipient can read/mark visible notifications; admin can create; no wrong-recipient read.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A user cannot mark or read a notification unless isNotificationVisibleToUser approves it.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin user; chat routes call participant-aware safe* helpers and attachment routes require caller/thread storage path prefix.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Only creator/user participants or admin support paths where intended can read or mutate chat state.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A non-participant cannot fetch a thread, send a message, mark read, hide, complete, or cancel another user's attachment.
auditTable.testRequired: chat route unit tests and validator.

auditTable.currentGuard: Participant or admin read; direct client writes false.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Realtime chat reads stay participant-scoped; all writes go through server routes.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A third user cannot attach a realtime listener to a creator/user conversation.

auditTable.currentGuard: Only creator/user pair can read; only creator or user can write their own uid child with validated typing/activeAt fields.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Realtime presence is participant-only and self-writable.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A non-participant cannot watch or spoof typing/presence for another chat pair.

auditTable.currentGuard: Authenticated trusted-origin user must have creator role and no drop submission restriction; creatorId is forced to caller.uid.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Creator actor only; creators can submit/edit only their own pending drops.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A creator cannot submit a drop as another creator because server overwrites creatorId and validates edit ownership.

auditTable.currentGuard: Public route returns active creator public profile fields and public-safe active drops only.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Guests can read creator public profile; private creator data remains excluded.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Creator private restrictions, payout, email, and identity document data are not returned in public profile response.
auditTable.testRequired: creator public page tests and validator.

auditTable.currentGuard: Legacy/manual cron adapters require CRON_SECRET bearer token plus rate limit.
auditTable.expectedGuard: System/server job only; public clients cannot trigger jobs.
auditTable.exploitScenario: A browser without the cron secret cannot process queue or notification jobs.

auditTable.currentGuard: Firebase scheduled functions, not public route handlers.
auditTable.expectedGuard: System/server job only.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Public clients cannot invoke scheduled materializers directly.

auditTable.currentGuard: Callable enforces App Check and authenticated request.auth.uid before writing authenticated analytics facts.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Authenticated user with App Check only; unknown actors cannot become authenticated users.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Unauthenticated or non-App-Check callers cannot write identified analytics facts.

auditTable.currentGuard: Validator scans use-client modules for server-only imports and non-public env vars.
auditTable.expectedGuard: Server secrets and Firebase Admin SDK stay out of client bundles.
auditTable.exploitScenario: Client bundles cannot import server-only code paths or read private env vars.
